front: The three rules of the Kubernetes network model
back: Every pod has its own IP; pods reach each other across nodes without NAT; node agents can reach pods on their node. A CNI plugin implements it.
A virtual IP allocated to a Service from the service CIDR. No interface owns it; kube-proxy rules DNAT connections to a Ready backend pod.
`port`: Service port for clients. `targetPort`: port (or named port) the pod listens on. `nodePort`: port opened on every node (30000–32767) for NodePort/LoadBalancer.

Objects listing a Service's backend IPs/ports with conditions `ready`, `serving`, `terminating`. Created by the EndpointSlice controller from the selector; linked by label `kubernetes.io/service-name`.
ClusterIP (internal), NodePort (port on every node), LoadBalancer (external LB via a cloud controller), ExternalName (DNS CNAME), headless (`clusterIP: None`, pod IPs in DNS).
No automatic endpoints; you create an EndpointSlice (label `kubernetes.io/service-name: <svc>`) pointing at any IPs, e.g. an external VM or database.
iptables (default, random-probability chains), nftables (stable since v1.33, successor), ipvs (deprecated since v1.35). eBPF CNIs like Cilium can replace kube-proxy.

front: Why don't long-lived connections rebalance across new pods?
back: Service load balancing picks a backend per connection (conntrack). HTTP/2, gRPC, DB pools and WebSockets keep one connection to one pod.
Cluster: any node forwards to any pod (even spread, extra hop, source IP lost). Local: only local pods serve (client IP preserved; nodes without pods drop traffic).
Names with fewer than 5 dots are tried with every search domain before being tried as-is, causing extra NXDOMAIN queries for external names. Fix with a trailing dot or lower `ndots`.
kube-proxy sends all connections from the same client IP to the same pod for `timeoutSeconds` (default 3 hours). Coarse; prefer stateless apps.
Run `cloud-provider-kind` (macOS: `sudo cloud-provider-kind --enable-lb-port-mapping`), then reach the `kindccm-*` container's mapped localhost port.
Pods Ready → EndpointSlice has addresses → targetPort correct → app listens on 0.0.0.0 → pod IP reachable → ClusterIP reachable → DNS resolves → NetworkPolicies.
`kubectl run netshoot --image=nicolaka/netshoot --rm -it --restart=Never -- bash`, or attach to a pod: `kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=nicolaka/netshoot --target=<container>`.
